highlights: # Tenstorrent hits $6.2B valuation to scale open-weight AI chips. Tenstorrent, a chip startup focused on inference, has raised $1.5 billion at a $6.2 billion valuation. The round comes five months after the 10-year-old Nvidia challenger reportedly received acquisition interest from Intel and Qualcomm at valuations of as much as $5 billion. The fresh round, which more than doubled Tenstorrent’s valuation from the $2.6 billion it fetched in late 2024, was led by Trace Capital, a new firm launched by Quiet Capital co-founder Ben Mahdavi, and Innovation X. The new capital will go toward scaling chips tailored for serving open-weight AI models and video generation. Tenstorrent is part of a wave of AI hardware startups trying to chip away at Nvidia’s dominance. Among them is Etched, an AI chip maker that was fielding investment offers at valuations of $40 billion or more, TechCrunch reported earlier this month. latest.title: Amazon is taking its biggest shot at Nvidia yet with new TorchNeuron dev tool - TechCrunch
latest.summary: On Monday, Amazon Web Services released a tool called TorchNeuron that lets AI startups easily move their AI apps onto Amazon’s AI chip, Trainium. In doing so, Amazon is also taking a direct stab at t...
highlights: On Monday, Amazon Web Services released a tool called TorchNeuron that lets AI startups easily move their AI apps onto Amazon’s AI chip, Trainium. In doing so, Amazon is also taking a direct stab at the the software advantage that has helped Nvidia become the default hardware choice for AI apps, and spurred its rise as AI hardware provider of choice. TorchNeuron works with PyTorch, a free, open-source toolkit that developers use to build, train, and run AI models. It lets AI apps written with PyTorch run on Trainium by changing just one line of configuration, according to Amazon — no code rewrite required. Nvidia has spent years ensuring its CUDA software — the software infrastructure that allows apps to run on Nvidia GPUs and its other hardware — seamlessly supports AI apps written with PyTorch. However, Amazon argues that porting to Trainium isn’t just easy; it also gives AI startups access to Amazon’s entire cloud.

week.title: Not Anthropic. Not OpenAI. This Is the Artificial Intelligence (AI) Stock I'd Buy Before the Next Mega-IPO. | The Motley Fool
week.summary: Anthropic's relationship with Google runs even deeper. In October 2025, Anthropic announced its use of Google's custom silicon, called Tensor Processing Units (TPUs). In April, this relationship was e...
highlights: Anthropic's relationship with Google runs even deeper. In October 2025, Anthropic announced its use of Google's custom silicon, called Tensor Processing Units (TPUs). In April, this relationship was expanded to include multiple gigawatts of TPU capacity expected to come online in 2027.

These arrangements create an attractive business model for Alphabet because the company can develop AI products for consumers while simultaneously supplying infrastructure that competing enterprises need. [...] The answer is simple: Alphabet is positioned to benefit from Anthropic's success in multiple ways. First, its equity investment will appreciate as Anthropic's valuation increases. Additionally, Anthropic is a major customer for Google's cloud infrastructure and custom AI chips. Third, Google's tie-up with Anthropic gives it exposure to an alternative AI ecosystem, reducing its dependence on Gemini emerging as the industry's go-to model. [...] One of Alphabet's quiet advantages is that it doesn't need its Gemini AI models to beat ChatGPT or Claude. That reason is Google Cloud provides compute infrastructure to its competitors. In May 2025, OpenAI agreed to use Google Cloud's capacity to train and deploy its AI models.

highlights: # roommaster Introduces AI Connector, Bringing Live Hotel PMS Data into ChatGPT, Claude, Microsoft Copilot and Google Gemini. **In Brief:** roommaster has launched AI Connector, a tool enabling live hotel PMS data to be accessed through generative AI platforms such as ChatGPT, Claude, Microsoft Copilot, and Google Gemini, allowing hotels to leverage conversational AI for operational queries and decision-making. * roommaster Introduces AI Connector, Bringing Live Hotel PMS Data into ChatGPT, Claude, Microsoft Copilot and Google Gemini - Image Credit roommaster. roommaster today announced the launch of **roommaster AI Connector**, a new integration that connects hotel property management system (PMS) data with leading AI assistants, including ChatGPT, Claude, Microsoft Copilot and Google Gemini. Available now for hotels using the latest upgraded version of roommaster PMS, the connector enables hotel teams to ask questions in natural language and retrieve relevant information from their live property management data. roommaster AI Connector introduces an alternative: hotel staff can ask questions in everyday language through a compatible AI assistant and retrieve relevant answers from their connected roommaster data.
